kiln_p05_001.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_001.text: The stairs above the archive creaked whenever a worker crossed the landing with full buckets. Yue noticed the sound while lifting the old supplier circular from its packet. The room smelled of dry paper, cold brick and a faint damp patch behind the lowest shelf. Peng had arranged the newest records well above that patch. The older failures remained where generations of keepers had placed them, beneath a stair that everybody used and nobody admired. Yue wondered how many decisions had been made upstairs without anyone descending to see the objects those decisions left behind.

kiln_p05_002.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_002.text: Peng opened the lower cupboard with an ordinary key. Inside stood jars of retained body, each holding less material than its outer size suggested. Labels peeled where old paste had become brittle. Yue read the shelf index before touching any jar. One matched the supplier circular's year; another matched the older reference cup whose successful programme had later been copied. The two bodies did not share a source or preparation note. Their names differed by one word. A copying clerk could miss the distinction without changing a single number on the firing slate.

kiln_p05_003.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_003.text: They carried only the authorised study jars to the cold comparison bench. The originals stayed closed until Luo could witness their condition. Yue used the waiting to examine the index's cross-references. A successful sample from that year had been loaned to an exhibition and never returned to this cupboard. Its receiving entry named the association's teaching room. The current reference vessel might descend from that sample line, but they would need the association's record to establish it. Peng sent the request. Yue resisted drawing a neat family tree for objects that had not yet agreed to their ancestry.

kiln_p05_004.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_004.text: Luo remembered the exhibition because he had worn borrowed shoes that pinched his toes. The successful cup had been made by a visiting specialist on a small shelf under unusually controlled conditions. It was not evidence that the ordinary workshop could produce hundreds under the cheaper schedule. Yue asked why the supplier circular sounded so confident. Luo said the writer wanted to sell body, while the exhibition wanted to sell admiration. Neither audience had asked enough about the ordinary work between a successful sample and a season of reliable production. The cup's beauty had done part of the persuading.

kiln_p05_005.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_005.text: Zhu brought her new trial dimensions while they discussed that old gap. She listened, then asked whether the successful specialist had left any process notes. The archive retained a rough forming card and a sketch of the shelf, but no complete drying history. They might learn from the sketch without claiming to reproduce its missing conditions. Zhu placed her current measured plan beside it. Her new cup looked less elegant. Its maker also knew which wall thickness she could repeat. Yue found herself admiring the plain plan more intensely than the absent exhibition piece.

kiln_p05_006.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_006.text: The first archive task was not interpretation but ordinary repair. A loose shelf peg had allowed the lowest board to lean toward the damp brick. Han replaced the peg while Yue held the empty board. Peng moved the covered records to a dry table and checked them afterward. No one used a spirit stone to persuade wood to remain strong. The replacement peg cost little and solved the actual support fault. Yue laughed when Han tapped it twice and announced a successful foundational breakthrough. Peng told him the peg's higher realms required a receipt.

kiln_p05_007.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_007.text: Behind the shelf they found a packet wrapped in an old wool scarf. Its cover listed unsuccessful trials whose makers had declined display. The scarf had protected the paper from dust but trapped some damp at one edge. Peng separated the dry leaves and called the town paper conservator for the stuck corner. Yue had hoped to unfold everything immediately. Waiting preserved more than curiosity could. She wrote the packet's place and condition in the index. The scarf smelled of smoke from a fire no current worker remembered, ordinary cloth carrying time without knowing what time meant.

kiln_p05_008.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_008.text: The conservator arrived with clean blotting sheets and the caution of a person frequently invited after damage had already been made worse. She used no qi on the fragile ink. Controlled ordinary drying and patient separation would take several days. Peng accepted the cost from the archive repair allowance. Tan asked whether the expense could wait until the teaching order paid. The keeper said the material was already at risk, and the teaching order had not been accepted. He nodded without arguing. Yue noticed how often the unaccepted order had become an imagined purse where a real one was needed.

kiln_p05_009.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_009.text: While the packet dried, Yue worked through the shelf sketches already safe to read. Several successes occupied the upper centre, where heat and air had been most even. The rejected mass-production estimate assumed the same result across a crowded full shelf. She overlaid the positions on a current cold arrangement and saw why the inference was weak. A small known success might be real without proving a large proposed promise. Zhu asked her to explain it to Jian. The boy understood when she placed one stool in the room and then tried to fit twenty around the same table.

kiln_p05_010.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_010.text: Jian added a twenty-first stool in the doorway and declared it the association's discount seat. Han sat on it and promptly blocked everyone's exit. Their demonstration ended in laughter and a useful removal. Yue drew the real shelf spacing afterward. Tan watched from the order-room door and said the estimate had priced the discount seat as if it occupied no floor. He was joking, but the joke identified a flaw he had once defended. Peng asked him to include actual permitted spacing in the next estimate. He took the measured drawing instead of the clever phrase.

kiln_p05_011.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_011.text: The town's ordinary noise returned around the drying papers: cart wheels, a saw from the carpenter's yard, children arguing over the puppet pot's verdict. Yue copied a margin note while the upper stairs shook under boots. She felt tempted to hurry because somebody was always passing. Then she realised that the archive's pace need not imitate the hall's busiest steps. A copied numeral would still be needed after the person above had left. She slowed the brush and left a blank where an ink stain hid part of the figure.

kiln_p05_012.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_012.text: The hidden figure could be checked against an original fuel issue sheet, if it survived. Peng led her to a drawer of ordinary stock records with handles polished by long use. Some sheets had been retained because an auditor once requested them; others had remained only because nobody had cleared the drawer. Yue found the matching issue and discovered that the successful exhibition trial used more sound charcoal per vessel than the later economical circular implied. The difference might include unused stock returned afterward. They searched for that return before treating issue weight as consumed heat.

kiln_p05_013.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_013.text: The return sheet survived in a neighbouring packet. It reduced the difference but did not erase it. More importantly, the old trial had used a longer interval and a smaller arrangement. Its resource history belonged to the actual success, not to a cheap promise copied from its photograph. Luo looked relieved to see the comparison written clearly. He had disliked the economical schedule for years without being able to explain why to a clerk holding an impressive sample. Yue wondered how many useful doubts had been dismissed because the doubter could offer only a feeling against a polished object.

kiln_p05_014.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_014.text: She took the ordinary evidence to Tan with Peng beside her. He read it, checked the arithmetic and asked why the old circular had never been corrected. Peng said the archive had not previously joined these records into the present question. The workshop could request correction now without pretending it had known all along. Tan wanted to accuse the association of hiding the fuel history. Yue asked which evidence showed that it had received the return sheet. He looked annoyed, then admitted none did. They would send the history and ask what supported its cheaper claim.

kiln_p05_015.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_015.text: The association answered with a printed trade booklet that repeated the circular's schedule. Its authority came from how often suppliers used it, not from a new trial report. Luo read the page aloud while Han trimmed an ordinary bowl. Every listener could hear the condition omitted between the old source and the new booklet. Han said a bowl copied often enough did not stop rocking. Zhu asked him to put that sentence in the workshop notice. He refused because somebody might expect him to make a less rocking bowl to accompany it.

kiln_p05_016.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_016.text: Peng laughed hard enough to lose her place in the index. Yue had rarely heard the keeper laugh without holding it behind her mouth. The sound made her seem younger, and then the laughter made her sing a foolish line while searching for the missing page. Her voice was confidently off key. Han groaned. Peng sang louder. Yue remembered the roommate's warning about terrible singing and enjoyed discovering that the archive's most precise keeper could offend an entire room with one musical note. The index returned to order; the song did not.

kiln_p05_017.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_017.text: After lunch, Peng explained that the bad song belonged to an old winter shift. Workers used it to keep time while carrying empty frames, with no live process depending on the rhythm. She had learned it as a junior keeper and never improved. Yue asked why the archive held failures but not songs. Peng looked surprised by the question. Songs lived in people until they did not. Perhaps a work-history note could preserve one without making it an instruction. Yue wrote the lyric in her private book, marking it as a memory rather than a timing method.

kiln_p05_018.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_018.text: The note made her think of the worker who had left after the old burn. The archive recorded treatment support and an ordinary wage statement, but little of his actual craft. Luo found a retained sound storage jar bearing the worker's maker mark. It stood in the tool room holding dry cord. They added its documented skill reference to the old training index without touching his private treatment cover. The person had made more than an incident. Yue felt the room become larger when a sound useful jar stood beside the failed shelf's account.

kiln_p05_019.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_019.text: Zhu approved that addition, then asked whether Yue planned to rescue every absent worker from every small description. Yue said she could not. She could try to stop one failure from becoming the only thing they knew about someone when more evidence lay within reach. Zhu nodded and returned to her current sample handles. The answer was modest enough to be useful. Yue had begun trusting modest answers because they left room for the next person to have a life beyond her explanation. Her desire to help no longer always required the centre of the scene.

kiln_p05_020.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_020.text: The fresh trial pieces dried under ordinary covers while rain moved through the fifth week. They weighed selected pieces at the prescribed intervals and compared the results with room conditions. Zhu would not let a surface feel decide the whole body. The earlier firing's density variation had made internal moisture and forming consistency worth closer study. She made one extra ordinary witness piece for destructive checking, funded within the revised small trial. The retained six cups stayed intact. Learning could cost a piece of clay, but the piece and the reason would be named before cutting.

kiln_p05_021.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_021.text: Han split the witness after its scheduled drying interval. The interior remained slightly darker near the thickened foot, though the outside seemed ready. They extended drying within the permitted plan rather than increase furnace heat to chase concealed water out of the finished cup. Yue thought of the old graceful drawing and wondered whether anyone had priced waiting. Tan checked the new agreement. It included development time rather than a fixed production month. He looked relieved and embarrassed again. An honest allowance for waiting had become something he could finally explain without inventing a delay penalty.

kiln_p05_022.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_022.text: Jian asked whether he could perform the next moisture comparison as a supervised learning task. Zhu agreed to teach the sample handling, with Han witnessing. The boy selected the correct piece and repeated the measurement after noticing a cloth weight in the tray. Yue smiled at the remembered error. He caught her smiling and accused her of enjoying his near mistake. She said she enjoyed watching him catch it. He accepted that distinction. The record described one bounded comparison task, not a mastery of all ceramic moisture or a claim that his fingers could now read the centre.

kiln_p05_023.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_023.text: At the end of the shift, Jian practised making handles beside Yue. His ordinary clay looked more willing than hers. He tried to help by taking her piece and fixing it. She stopped him with an embarrassed laugh. She wanted to learn the movement, not own a good handle made by him. He returned the clay and showed her the join slowly. The exchange reminded Yue of Zhu's tray after the failed shelf. Help could quietly replace the person it intended to support. This time they found a useful shape before anybody had to feel wounded by kindness.

kiln_p05_024.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_024.text: Tan came to inspect the actual drying schedule with his coat unbuttoned, having walked quickly from the association office. The printed booklet's editor had agreed to review the omitted condition but asked for a certified account of the current failure. Peng sent the retained evidence list and separated the ordinary firing faults from the later discharge test. The editor wanted one simple reason for the correction. Luo said there were several supported reasons. A simple trade warning could name the unproved extension without pretending the entire shelf had failed from one universal cause.

kiln_p05_025.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_025.text: The association's local agent visited again, less polished after rain marked his boots. He asked whether the workshop intended to damage the supplier's reputation. Zhu asked whether naming an unsupported schedule damaged its reputation more than putting it into four hundred cups. He did not like the answer. Peng kept the conversation with the evidence rather than let it become a competition in sharpness. The proposed correction would say that the storage schedule's extension to this teaching design remained unproved. No accusation of concealed intent would be printed merely because the omission was expensive.

kiln_p05_026.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_026.text: After the agent left, Zhu said she regretted the sharp question only a little. Yue admitted that she had wanted to say something worse. Han pointed out that both would have been less memorable if spoken through a mouthful of bread. They ate the late meal together. The tension loosened in ordinary crumbs. Yue found she could enjoy a friend being imperfect without turning imperfection into proof the friend was secretly wrong about everything. Zhu's sharpness did not make the schedule sound. The agent's irritation did not make him incapable of carrying a useful correction.

kiln_p05_027.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_027.text: The conservator separated the last stuck leaves on the sixth day. One contained a private apprentice's account of the old exhibition trial, shared for teaching under the keeper's retained permission note. It described a full day spent adjusting the successful cup's foot, followed by a longer drying interval than the later circular allowed. The writer complained about cold fingers and praised the visiting specialist's patience. Yue loved the ungrand detail. The celebrated success had been made by people who were uncomfortable, uncertain and still willing to wait until the material was ready.

kiln_p05_028.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_028.text: The apprentice's account also named a failed first shelf, discarded before the exhibition photograph was taken. The retained failures packet contained two small fragments from it, each with a matching position note. The successful cup had followed an ordinary setback and a revision. Yue looked at the circular's smooth story of efficient production and felt angry on the forgotten shelf's behalf. Peng reminded her that the fragments were evidence, not people asking for revenge. Yue laughed at herself and wrote the revision sequence. Success had a history, and omitting that history could make the next maker spend it again.

kiln_p05_029.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_029.text: Luo compared the old revised foot with Zhu's new measured design. They differed, but the old note helped explain why thicker lower walls needed patient drying and a suitable cooling interval. The kiln could use the lesson without claiming to reproduce an absent specialist's full method. Zhu revised one trial dimension before the cups entered final drying. She remade the affected pieces rather than trim wet clay into a false match. The revision used the planned development stock and left its ordinary failed practice pieces in the reclaim stream. No unpaid apprentice batch quietly supplied the change.

kiln_p05_030.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_030.text: Yue asked Peng why the failures packet had been placed so low beneath the stairs. The keeper said she did not know the original decision. Display preferences, limited room and later habit could all have contributed. They would move the retained current trial histories into a more findable index, but first they needed to preserve the actual packet order for the old inquiry. Yue accepted the slower improvement. It was tempting to reorganise evidence into a story she liked before understanding why its pieces had become scattered. A clearer shelf should not manufacture a clearer past.

kiln_p05_031.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_031.text: That evening Peng invited Yue to her small rented room to review the apprentice account's authorised teaching extract. A chipped ordinary bowl held pins on the windowsill. The keeper had been sewing another record cover and had stabbed her thumb twice. Yue took the needle while Peng read the source aloud. Her stitches were uneven, but the cover held. They talked about work without the hall listening. Peng said she had once dreamed of leaving for a mountain school. Yue asked what stopped her. Peng smiled. Leaving had not been the only way to find a larger task.

kiln_p05_032.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_032.text: Yue felt embarrassed by how quickly she had imagined the answer would be a lost chance. Peng enjoyed the archive, its difficult questions and the people whose work it kept. She also resented parts of it and sometimes wanted a different life. Those feelings did not require a single verdict. Yue told her about the letter to her mother and the kiln labor she had failed to notice as a child. Peng listened, then asked whether the cover had been sewn backward. It had. They laughed and unpicked the last seam together.

kiln_p05_033.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_033.text: On the walk back upstairs, Yue carried the authorised extract and her own less elegant cover. The passage smelled of bread cooling after the night's bake. She stopped at the door long enough to hear her roommates arguing about whose socks had survived the pipe repair best. Her life in the town had accumulated ordinary attachments while the next-stage letter travelled. She no longer pictured cultivation as a straight road that became clearer whenever other people stepped out of it. The road passed through work, and through people who might prefer not to travel at all.

kiln_p05_034.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_034.text: The next morning, Peng proposed a small teaching display of authorised failed trials. It would show a process sequence rather than an exhibition of makers' shame. Zhu wanted the current failed sample's material and discharge notes included, with no private treatment history attached. Han offered his absurd early handle on the condition that the caption admit it had taught him something. Luo contributed an ordinary warped jar from his first year. Jian asked whether his sliced foot could stand beside them. The keeper agreed after recording which pieces belonged to current study and which were personal loans.

kiln_p05_035.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_035.text: Yue made the display plan with too many words. The first card tried to explain the complete contract dispute, both body histories and the nature of honest failure. Zhu read half of it and said a visitor would die of old age before reaching the handle. They reduced each card to the relevant task, observed fault and useful next question. Longer source notes stayed in the study folder. The display became clearer without becoming falsely simple. Yue enjoyed deleting a sentence she had secretly admired. It freed room for an object the visitor could actually inspect.

kiln_p05_036.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_036.text: The shelf stood in the cold visitor passage, beyond the working hall's clear route. The public could look without approaching live firing or restricted records. Peng borrowed a plain barrier cord, which Jian immediately asked whether anyone might mistake for a hand rail. They fixed it higher and added a solid ordinary rail at the corner. Han called this the display's first failed trial. Yue kept the correction in their setup note and did not turn it into another card. The exhibit needed to work, not prove that its makers had become incapable of initial mistakes.

kiln_p05_037.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_037.text: On the first open afternoon, a visiting potter laughed at Luo's warped jar. Then he turned it to see the bottom and became serious. He had made the same error on a much larger batch. He asked about the revised cooling interval, and Luo showed him the authorised public extract. The visitor offered a comparison from his own body, clearly a different method rather than a universal cure. Yue watched an embarrassed laugh become a useful technical conversation. The failed jar had done more work in ten minutes than it had done hidden behind the tool cupboard for years.

kiln_p05_038.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_038.text: A woman from one of the beginner classes examined the guarded discharge sample through its clear cover. She asked whether a cup could look sound and still be unsuitable for instruction. Zhu said yes and showed the plain note describing the release difference. The woman became angry because she had always been told a cracked-looking vessel was the only one to refuse. The association instructor, attending the display, listened and explained the actual inspection and grounded-release rules used in her room. Yue was glad the correction came from the person responsible for teaching rather than from a traveler collecting indignation.

kiln_p05_039.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_039.text: The instructor promised to review the room's ordinary briefing and retain the source note. She did not declare every older cup dangerous. Each needed assessment under its actual method and history. The woman asked to see that history for the class set, and the instructor agreed to bring the authorised records next week. Their conversation was less satisfying than a dramatic condemnation and more useful to the learners who would return there. Yue found herself choosing useful more often, though she still felt the pull of a scene with an obvious final line.

kiln_p05_040.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_040.text: Children preferred Han's handle. They claimed it resembled a rabbit, a frightened minister and an ear growing out of a cabbage. Han defended its dignity until one child asked whether the current better handle was also available to see. He fetched a sound ordinary practice example and let them compare the join cold. Their fingers learned the difference faster than they learned his captions. Yue added a simple drawing of the correct join beside the comic one. Han demanded the rabbit receive equal credit. Peng offered it a personal-loan label and no wage.

kiln_p05_041.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_041.text: The public shelf drew one angry supplier clerk. He said the display made prepared body look dishonest. Yue showed him the card, which distinguished permitted sorted reclaim for ordinary ware from unproved suitability for thin charged teaching vessels. He admitted the wording was narrower than the rumor he had heard. He still disliked the mention of the failed particle. Luo offered to attach the supplier's actual screen specification when it arrived, without deleting the observed fault. The clerk accepted the offer reluctantly. Reputation could answer evidence by supplying better evidence, rather than by requiring the object to disappear.

kiln_p05_042.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_042.text: Tan feared the display would frighten purchasers away. Then the bakery owner arrived with a request for six ordinary chalk cups and laughed at the guarded pickle suggestion in Han's private joke. A farmer asked about sound broad-footed jars for winter seed storage. Neither needed charged teaching ware. They wanted useful ordinary things and liked seeing how the workshop checked them. Tan took both inquiries with real dimensions and no borrowed production month. The display had not magically paid the kiln's debts. It had reminded the town that the hall made more than one difficult proposed object.

kiln_p05_043.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_043.text: That evening the owner approved a small budget for improving the archive's ordinary storage, separate from commission development. The money bought dry covers, sound shelf pegs and a simple index board. Peng declined an ornate cabinet offered by a merchant. It would cost more, hold less and fit badly beneath the stair. Yue helped carry the plain boards while Han measured the new height. The work smelled of fresh wood instead of old damp. She liked the improvement's modest solidity. Nobody needed a higher realm to make the next reader's ordinary search less difficult.

kiln_p05_044.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_044.text: While sorting for the new shelves, Yue found two copies of the economical circular with different margin notes. One questioned the extension to thin teaching ware. The other replaced the question mark with a neat approval stroke, but its attached test reference led back to the small exhibition sample. The stroke had been made years later by a temporary contracts officer. No one current had signed it. Tan recognised the copying habit: people turned a resolved commercial question into an apparently resolved technical one. The officer had approved the price proposal, not proven the crowded firing programme.

kiln_p05_045.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_045.text: They could establish that interpretation from the officer's covering letter, which discussed cost and market interest without claiming a new trial. The approval stroke had travelled without the cover. Yue made a linked copy of both documents. Peng sent the association the supported distinction, asking it to amend the proposal's reference. She did not ask the agent to confess an intent that belonged to no retained evidence. Tan read the note and said it would be harder to argue against than the accusation he had first wanted. Yue was pleased, then cautious about being pleased by her own restraint.

kiln_p05_046.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_046.text: Luo asked why caution made her look ashamed. Yue admitted that part of her wanted the agent to be a villain, because then the workshop could be innocent. Luo laughed without delight. The workshop had copied the same unproved programme when it hoped for affordable winter work. A villain would have been convenient for him too. He tapped the cold slate and said they still needed a sound next firing. Moral clarity might improve a conversation. It could not replace the actual cup's drying record. Yue returned to the sample bench with a less theatrical kind of resolve.

kiln_p05_047.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_047.text: The revised pieces reached their ordinary readiness checks near the end of the fifth week. Their witness piece no longer showed the earlier dark centre after the extended drying interval. Zhu recorded the result with the room conditions and kept it linked to the changed thickness. The cups were not identical to the failed first set. That was the point of the revision, and it limited what could be inferred from comparison. Yue wrote the distinction without apologising for the need to learn. The next trial would test this revised set, not retroactively prove the old one should have survived.

kiln_p05_048.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_048.text: At the cold setup, Jian caught a copied position number that matched two cups. Zhu checked the maker record and corrected the second tag before placement. The original clerical error remained readable. Jian looked pleased enough to burst. Luo asked him to explain why the correction mattered. The boy described how later defects might otherwise be assigned to the wrong air position. Yue could hear the answer come from actual work rather than memorised caution. They recorded the exercise as part of his current supervised comparison task. His learning had begun to give him reasons beyond wanting a larger number.

kiln_p05_049.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_049.text: The warning checks worked under the present rain and closed-room conditions. The repaired lintel kept the handover station dry. Luo inspected the fuel and measuring supply, then assigned the actual occupied posts. Yue had slept properly, eaten and remained within her established route allowance, but her task still used ordinary observation only. She did not resent that choice today. The sample's success would belong to the material, making and crew process, not to a hidden personal boost she could claim after the fact. She tied back her sleeves and set the slate where her hand could reach it comfortably.

kiln_p05_050.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_050.text: The revised ordinary firing proceeded more slowly through the interval that had troubled the first shelf. Luo used the planned wider air space and the body-specific development schedule funded for this trial. The lower and upper witnesses remained within the permitted comparison. Han fed ordinary charcoal while Jian maintained the assigned handover marks. Yue recorded the observations and noticed how tempted she was to call steady readings success. She waited. The cups still needed cooling and inspection. The kiln's calm sound helped her endure that unfinished answer without making the answer prematurely complete.

kiln_p05_051.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_051.text: During a late heating interval, a delivery cart arrived with a damaged wheel. Its driver shouted for help across the yard. The crew did not abandon occupied posts. Peng arranged ordinary assistance from workers outside the live firing assignment, and the driver stopped beside the gate. Yue heard the commotion without moving from her station. She wanted to be useful everywhere and could not. The handover responsibility in front of her was already useful. Later she learned that the cart held cloth, not fuel, and nobody was injured. The story's lack of drama felt like a gift.

kiln_p05_052.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_052.text: At supper, Jian asked whether she had wished for a crisis she could solve. Yue almost denied it. She had wished for no crisis, but if one came she wanted not to be irrelevant. The boy understood the difference too well. He said he hated waiting for adults to decide whether his work counted. Yue asked whether the new task records had changed that feeling. He said they helped until somebody stopped following them. She could offer no final cure for distrust. She offered the next concrete review date, and the ridiculous title Lord of the Steady Interval.

kiln_p05_053.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_053.text: He rejected the title because steadiness sounded old. Han accepted it on his behalf and proposed a ceremony involving sweeping the bench. The boy retaliated by appointing Han Emperor of the Missing Tooth. Zhu declared the ceremony closed before royalty damaged any actual cups. The laughter was coarse, affectionate and badly timed for Tan's incoming letter. He waited until they finished rather than demand attention with a serious face. When he read the letter, the association had agreed to correct the schedule reference. It wanted a new production estimate after the revised sample result. The harder commercial argument was approaching.

kiln_p05_054.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_054.text: Peng checked the unused large-order advance once more with the owner. It remained intact under the amended conditional receipt. If the new estimate was refused, returning it would cost ordinary messenger and transfer fees already allowed in the agreement. Tan did not have to invent a miracle commission to avoid an impossible repayment. He looked almost disappointed by how ordinary the path out could be. Yue understood. A dramatic rescue might have let him feel powerful after months of debt. Correcting an account let him remain employed and responsible, which was a quieter form of dignity.

kiln_p05_055.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_055.text: The ordinary cooled inspection took place the following day. Four revised cups passed the specified cold checks, one showed an unacceptable handle join and one had a minor rim distortion. The crew retained the passing group for the guarded method-specific evaluation; none entered a class immediately. Zhu compared the defects with her forming notes and found where one join had dried differently. She accepted the result without declaring the whole redesign either vindicated or useless. The new shelf had learned something real. It still contained objects that would not become safe teaching vessels by being needed.

kiln_p05_056.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_056.text: Yue inspected the sound four under the changed lamp angle, repeating the viewing method that had found the first shelf's hidden line. She missed nothing evident within the prescribed checks, but she did not write that nothing could be wrong. The next guarded release test would answer another defined question. Han said her wording had become shorter and less afraid. She was pleased. Her caution no longer needed a paragraph to announce its virtue. It could become a clear action: turn the cup, check the foot, record the observed condition and let the next assessor do the next task.

kiln_p05_057.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_057.text: Zhu sent her new result to the specialist the association had funded for the release review. The specialist would arrive with the instructor after the next ordinary rest day. Their review concerned the revised geometry and established modest demonstration method, not a new kind of unlimited artifact. Luo held the group in guarded storage while the workshop completed paid ordinary jar work. Yue helped the crew switch tasks and found it easier than leaving the first sample firing. A promising cup could wait. The people who needed ordinary seed jars should not wait solely because a teaching vessel was interesting.

kiln_p05_058.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_058.text: On the rest day, Yue and Zhu walked beyond the market to a low hill overlooking the kiln roofs. Cold grass cracked beneath their boots. Zhu carried no tool tray, and Yue left her study slate upstairs. The town looked less complicated from above: smoke, crooked lanes, a pale river beyond the fields. Then Zhu named three households in the nearest lane and the view became crowded with real lives again. Yue admitted that she often preferred a map because it did not ask anything of her. Zhu said maps waited until travelers forgot they were incomplete.

kiln_p05_059.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_059.text: They sat on a fallen ordinary wall, eating bread and sharp pickled greens. Yue asked whether Zhu wanted to study a new craft skill now that the old record was repaired. Zhu said perhaps glaze mixing, if it could fit her hand and paid duties. She did not need a grand new ambition to justify being grateful. Yue had expected the correction to release an entire future at once. Zhu laughed at that expectation. "You keep trying to make my life turn a page on your schedule," she said. Yue laughed too, this time before being hurt by the truth.

kiln_p05_060.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_060.text: At the hill's lower path, they found Jian examining a broken wooden toy cart. He had returned to the maker and bought a damaged one cheaply for repair practice. He looked embarrassed to be seen with it. Zhu asked about the axle instead of the price. The boy showed them how the straight joint worked and where the thin wood had split. Yue offered to hold it while he fitted a simple replacement pin at the lodging table. He accepted. The toy would carry no household wage and earn no institutional credit. It was still allowed to matter.

kiln_p05_061.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_061.text: That evening Jian repaired the cart while Yue held the body steady. Han provided a small piece of suitable ordinary wood from the permitted scrap box. The boy kept the axle free enough to turn and grinned when the cart rolled across the table. He planned to send it to his brother after testing it on the rough floor. Yue asked whether its successful table trial proved it could cross the desert. Jian threw a clean cloth at her. They had learned enough caution to mock its misuse. The cloth landed beside the private joke book and damaged no evidence.

kiln_p05_062.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_062.text: Peng brought a late note from Su Yan confirming her arrival at the beginning of the sixth week. The examiner wanted to inspect the comparison room before hearing any new-route request. She would review the work history and current ordinary recovery, then decide what supervision she could actually provide. Yue's stomach tightened with hope. The kiln's failed shelves had taught her not to confuse a desired answer with a prepared process. Even so, she laid out her own record twice and imagined how the next two pairs might feel, then stopped imagining before sensation became evidence.

kiln_p05_063.speaker: narrator
kiln_p05_063.text: She slept well and rose to ordinary breakfast. The day ahead contained guarded cup review, current archive work and the arrival of a teacher who already knew some of her impatience. None of those things required her to become fifth stage before the bell rang. She touched the repaired cover she and Peng had sewn and put it beside the actual fourth-stage record. Under the stair, the archive had kept the failed shelves long enough for their missing time to become useful. Yue wanted to learn a mastery that could do the same with her own mistakes.
